stories.body: President Donald Trump again said the United States has “total control” of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iranian authorities maintained that Washington must meet Tehran’s demands. The competing claims underscore continuing tension over the strategically vital waterway.
stories.headline: US and Iran exchange rival claims over control of the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: Rescuers in Colombia are approaching the critical 72-hour window for finding survivors after the country’s strongest earthquake this century. The magnitude 7.4 quake has killed at least 265 people, injured more than 3,500 and left nearly 500 missing, while more than 9,550 homes have been destroyed. Officials say the search has entered its final phase, though crews continue listening for signs of life beneath collapsed buildings in cities including Pereira and Cali. President Abelardo de La Espriella has promised an emergency fund to rebuild damaged homes, hospitals, schools and infrastructure.
stories.headline: Colombia earthquake rescue effort enters final phase as death toll reaches 265

stories.body: Russia struck the area around Ukraine’s Danube port of Izmail overnight, damaging infrastructure and starting a fire, regional authorities said. Ukraine, meanwhile, launched a major drone and missile attack on the Russian port of Novorossiysk, reportedly damaging grain-export terminals and the Black Sea Fleet’s remaining major base; Ukraine said four Russian warships were hit. Russian officials reported three deaths, including an eight-year-old child, and 24 injuries in the Novorossiysk attack, while Moscow said it had downed 362 Ukrainian drones and reported a refinery fire in Salavat.
stories.headline: Russian attacks hit Ukraine's Izmail port infrastructure as Kyiv targets Russian sites

stories.body: Zambians are voting in a general election in which President Hakainde Hichilema is widely expected to win a second term, despite voter frustration over living costs. His main challenge comes from the Tonse Alliance, led by former government chief whip Brian Mundubile. The campaign has been shaped by the continuing political legacy of Hichilema’s late rival, Edgar Lungu, including a dispute over Lungu’s burial, as well as opposition accusations that authorities have disrupted rallies and detained campaign workers. The government denies repression and says the opposition can campaign freely.
stories.headline: Zambia votes in election expected to return President Hichilema amid cost-of-living concerns

stories.body: The World Health Organization says the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is on course to surpass the 2014-16 West African epidemic as the deadliest ever if its current pace continues. More than 4,300 cases and 2,000 deaths have been recorded since the outbreak was declared in May, though genetic evidence indicates transmission began in February. The outbreak involves the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists, and containment has been hindered by conflict, poor access, weak health infrastructure, misinformation and unpaid health workers. WHO hopes to bring transmission under control within three months, while warning that this would not mean the outbreak had ended.
stories.headline: WHO warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak could become the deadliest on record

stories.body: Oil leaking from the grounded tanker Caroline Bezengi has reached beaches at Ras Madrakah on Oman’s mainland, contaminating up to 40 kilometres of coastline, the country’s Environment Authority said. The slick is also expected to reach the southern coast of Masirah Island and threatens environmentally sensitive waters around the Hallaniyat archipelago, where a marine reserve protects sea turtles and other wildlife. The vessel has been disabled since a reported explosion on June 8 and may hold about 800,000 barrels of crude. Western governments have identified it as part of Russia’s sanctioned shadow fleet.
stories.headline: Oil from a grounded tanker reaches Oman's mainland beaches

stories.body: Israeli settlers have continued to besiege Palestinian families in the West Bank village of Qusra, cutting off water, electricity and access to essential supplies. Residents say the siege began on Sunday and is intended to force them from their land; families inside say food supplies are running low. Israeli forces briefly dismantled a settler tent and clashed with some of the group but later withdrew, leaving settlers at the site. The Israeli military has described the seizure of Palestinian homes and land as illegal and unacceptable and says it will deploy an additional infantry battalion to the area.
stories.headline: Israeli settlers continue siege of Palestinian homes in the West Bank

stories.body: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to spend between $10 million and $20 million on gloves that can deliver electric shocks, prompting criticism from Democratic officials and civil-rights groups. The Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter, or GLOVE, is activated by a button and must contact bare skin to deliver a painful shock intended to gain compliance from resisting people. The gloves can deliver up to 380 volts and record activations through built-in microprocessors. The Department of Homeland Security said ICE is assessing equipment needs to ensure officers can safely make arrests and removals, while critics warned that the devices could be misused.
stories.headline: ICE plan to equip officers with electric-shock gloves draws criticism

stories.body: Police in Minnesota say a 41-year-old man killed his wife and their seven-year-old daughter at the Hopkins home where she operated a daycare, then died by suicide. Investigators also suspect he killed a 78-year-old female relative in a separate attack. Authorities said the man stabbed his wife and child before fatally shooting himself.
stories.headline: Minnesota man kills wife and daughter at daycare after killing another relative

stories.body: Severe storms have brought tornadoes, heavy rain, flash flooding and damage across parts of the US Midwest. Flooded neighborhoods in the Indianapolis metropolitan area have seen roads collapse into sinkholes, while communities in Ohio, Indiana and around Cincinnati have reported extensive flood and storm damage. Authorities have also reported deaths as the severe-weather outbreak continues to affect the region.
stories.headline: Severe Midwest weather brings tornadoes, flash flooding, deaths and damage

stories.body: Spain estimates that up to 5,000 people who arrived in Ceuta during the recent migration crisis could require reception: about 2,500 minors and 2,500 potential asylum seekers. Morocco is reinforcing the border with Ceuta after social-media calls for another mass crossing, following the late-July arrival of roughly 72,000 people and reported deaths on both sides of the border. Spain’s government is preparing a meeting with regional authorities focused on approving financial aid for Ceuta, including a proposed €25 million for the care of minors, while postponing debate over their distribution among regions and prioritising family reunification.
stories.headline: Ceuta migration crisis prompts dispute between Spain's government, opposition and Morocco

stories.body: A wildfire that began near Niebla in Huelva province a week ago has affected more than 31,000 hectares across Huelva and Seville, with a perimeter of about 120 kilometres, according to Spain’s Defence Ministry. More than 800 residents have been evacuated, and over 800 personnel, 26 aircraft and hundreds of military personnel are involved in the response. Authorities say the fire remains beyond extinguishing capacity because of low humidity, intense ground heating, shifting winds, convective conditions and secondary fires that have spread even against the wind.
stories.headline: Andalusia wildfire enters seventh day, affecting more than 31,000 hectares

stories.body: A Madrid judge has transferred his investigation into alleged efforts by former Socialist Party member Leire Díez to obtain compromising information on judges, anti-corruption prosecutors and Civil Guard officers to Spain’s National Court. Judge Arturo Zamarriego accepted a request by National Court magistrate Santiago Pedraz, who is already examining a broader alleged scheme to undermine judicial proceedings affecting the Socialist Party, the government and people close to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Díez, businessman Javier Pérez Dolset and journalist Pere Rusiñol had been placed under investigation in the Madrid case.
stories.headline: Spain's National Court takes over investigation into alleged Leire Díez scheme

stories.body: An electrical failure at the air traffic control tower at Barcelona-El Prat airport temporarily halted all flight operations for 15 minutes and caused delays and cancellations throughout the day. Although Aena said power had been fully restored during the afternoon, disruptions continued into the evening, especially for arriving flights. Ten of 1,124 scheduled operations were diverted to airports including Reus and Girona, while more than 20 arrivals and five departures were cancelled. Ryanair said almost 6,000 of its passengers were affected.
stories.headline: Electrical failure at El Prat air traffic control tower causes delays and cancellations

stories.body: Barcelona is expected to face another day of intense heat and oppressive humidity, with temperatures potentially reaching or exceeding 35°C in some parts of the city. Nighttime conditions are expected to remain exceptionally warm, with minimum temperatures around 29°C in central Barcelona from Thursday into Friday, making sleep difficult. The heat is forecast to continue through Friday and Saturday, though weather models indicate that more normal conditions may begin to return from Sunday.
stories.headline: Barcelona faces intensifying heat, with temperatures above 35°C and exceptionally hot nights

stories.body: Barcelona’s metro will operate continuously for 67 hours from 5am on Friday, August 21, until midnight on Sunday, August 23, to support the final weekend of the Gràcia Festival. Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona will also increase service on Line 3 by up to 10% at some times and deploy additional customer-service, security and cleaning staff at busy stations. The operator recommends using metro stations including Lesseps, Fontana, Diagonal, Joanic and Verdaguer to reach festival events and advises passengers to plan ahead because of ongoing summer works on the network.
stories.headline: Barcelona Metro to run continuously for 67 hours during Gràcia Festival
